title.zh: 卷一百〇七 列傳第五十七: 玄宗諸子
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 列傳第五十七: 玄宗諸子 Volume 111 Biographies 57: Xuanzong's Sons

sentences.zh: 玄宗三十子：元獻楊皇后生肅宗，劉華妃生奉天皇帝琮、靖恭太子琬、儀王璲，趙麗妃生廢太子瑛，錢妃生棣王琰，皇甫德儀生鄂王瑤，劉才人生光王琚，貞順武皇后生夏悼王一、懷哀王敏、壽王瑁、盛王琦，高婕妤生潁王璬、郭順儀生永王璘，柳婕妤生延王玢，鐘美人生濟王環，盧美人生信王瑝，閻才人生義王玭，王美人生陳王珪，陳美人生豐王珙，鄭才人生恆王瑱，武賢儀生涼王璿，汴哀王璥，余七王早夭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons: Empress Yuanxian of the Yang clan bore Suzong; Consort Liu Hua bore the Fengtian Emperor Cong, the Jinggong Heir Apparent Wan, and Prince of Yi Lin; Consort Zhao Li bore the deposed Crown Prince Ying; Consort Qian bore Prince of Di Yan; Lady Huangfu Deyi bore Prince of E Yao; Lady Liu bore Prince of Guang Ju; Empress Zhenshun Wu bore Prince Xia Ci Yi, Prince Huai'ai Min, Prince of Shou Mao, and Prince of Sheng Qi; Lady Gao bore Prince of Ying Li; Lady Guo Shunyi bore Prince of Yong Lin; Lady Liu bore Prince of Yan Bin; Lady Zhong bore Prince of Ji Huan; Lady Lu bore Prince of Xin Huang; Lady Yan bore Prince of Yi Ni; Lady Wang bore Prince of Chen Gui; Lady Chen bore Prince of Feng Gong; Lady Zheng bore Prince of Heng Zhen; Lady Wu Xianyi bore Prince of Liang Xuan and Prince of Bian Aihuan Jin; the other seven princes died young in infancy.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had thirty sons. Empress Yuanxian of the Yang clan was the mother of Suzong. Consort Liu Hua bore the Fengtian Emperor Cong, the Jinggong Heir Apparent Wan, and Prince of Yi Lin. Consort Zhao Li bore the deposed Crown Prince Ying; Consort Qian, Prince of Di Yan; Lady Huangfu Deyi, Prince of E Yao; Lady Liu, Prince of Guang Ju. Empress Zhenshun Wu bore Prince Xia Ci Yi, Prince Huai'ai Min, Prince of Shou Mao, and Prince of Sheng Qi. Lady Gao bore Prince of Ying Li; Lady Guo Shunyi, Prince of Yong Lin; Lady Liu, Prince of Yan Bin; Lady Zhong, Prince of Ji Huan; Lady Lu, Prince of Xin Huang; Lady Yan, Prince of Yi Ni; Lady Wang, Prince of Chen Gui; Lady Chen, Prince of Feng Gong; Lady Zheng, Prince of Heng Zhen; Lady Wu Xianyi, Prince of Liang Xuan and Prince of Bian Aihuan Jin. The remaining seven princes died in early childhood.

sentences.zh: 廢太子瑛，玄宗第二子也，本名嗣謙。

translations.literal: The deposed Crown Prince Ying was Emperor Xuanzong's second son; his original name was Siqian.
translations.idiomatic: The deposed Crown Prince Ying was Xuanzong's second son; his birth name was Siqian.

sentences.zh: 景雲元年九月，封真定郡王。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the first year of Jingyun, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhending commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of Jingyun 1 (710), he was created Prince of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 先天元年八月，進封郢王。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xiantian, he was advanced to Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xiantian 1 (712), he was promoted to Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 開元三年正月，立為皇太子。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year of Kaiyuan, he was installed as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Kaiyuan 3 (715), he was named crown prince.

sentences.zh: 七年正月，加元服。

translations.literal: In the first month of the seventh year, he received the cap of full manhood.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of that year (Kaiyuan 7), he underwent the coming-of-age ceremony.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄宗又令太子詣國子學行齒胄之禮，仍敕右散騎常侍褚無量升筵講論，學官及文武百官節級加賜。

translations.literal: That same year, Xuanzong also ordered the crown prince to go to the Directorate of Education to perform the ceremony of taking rank among the students in caps; he further commanded the Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry Chu Wuliang to ascend the dais and lecture, and the academic officials and civil and military officials all received graded additional rewards.
translations.idiomatic: That year Xuanzong also had the crown prince visit the Imperial Academy to perform the ceremony of taking his place among the capped students. He ordered Chu Wuliang, Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, to mount the lectern and discourse, and granted stepped bonuses to the academic officials and to the civil and military officers.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改名鴻，納妃薛氏，禮畢，曲赦京城之內，侍講潘肅等並加級改職，中書令蕭嵩親迎，特封徐國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was renamed Hong. He took Lady Xue as consort; when the rites were completed, a partial amnesty was proclaimed within the capital. Lecturers such as Pan Su were all promoted in rank and transferred in office. Chief Minister Xiao Song personally went to welcome the bride, and Ying was specially enfeoffed as Duke of Xu.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 he was renamed Hong. After he took Lady Xue as his consort and the wedding rites were finished, the court proclaimed a partial amnesty for the capital. Lecturers including Pan Su were promoted and reassigned. Chief Minister Xiao Song went in person to welcome the bride, and Ying was specially created Duke of Xu.

sentences.zh: 二十五年七月，改名瑛。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year, he was renamed Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 25 (737), he was renamed Ying.

sentences.zh: 瑛母趙麗妃，本伎人，有才貌，善歌舞，玄宗在潞州得幸。

translations.literal: Ying's mother, Consort Zhao Li, had originally been a performing artist; she had talent and beauty and was skilled in song and dance. Xuanzong favored her when he was in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ying's mother, Consort Zhao Li, had been a performer. Gifted and beautiful, she excelled at song and dance, and won Xuanzong's favor while he was in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 及景雲升儲之後，其父元禮、兄常奴擢為京職，開元初皆至大官。

translations.literal: After he was raised as heir apparent in the Jingyun era, her father Yuanli and her brother Changnu were promoted to capital offices; in the early Kaiyuan years both reached high rank.
translations.idiomatic: After Ying was named heir apparent in the Jingyun era, her father Yuanli and her brother Changnu were given posts in the capital, and by the early Kaiyuan period both had risen to high office.

sentences.zh: 及武惠妃寵幸，麗妃恩乃漸弛。

translations.literal: When Consort Wu Hui gained favor, Consort Li's grace gradually slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Once Consort Wu Hui won the emperor's favor, Consort Li's standing gradually waned.

sentences.zh: 時鄂王瑤母皇甫德儀、光王琚母劉才人，皆玄宗在臨淄邸以容色見顧，出子朗秀而母加愛焉。

translations.literal: At that time the mothers of Prince of E Yao, Lady Huangfu Deyi, and Prince of Guang Ju, Lady Liu, had both been noticed for their looks when Xuanzong was at the Linzi residence; their sons were bright and handsome, and their mothers received added affection.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of E Yao's mother, Lady Huangfu Deyi, and Prince of Guang Ju's mother, Lady Liu, had both caught Xuanzong's eye for their beauty when he was still at the Linzi mansion. Their sons were handsome and bright, and their mothers were favored all the more.

sentences.zh: 及惠妃承恩，鄂、光之母亦漸疏薄，惠妃之子壽王瑁，鐘愛非諸子所比。

translations.literal: When Consort Hui received favor, the mothers of Princes of E and Guang also grew gradually distant and slighted; Consort Hui's son, Prince of Shou Mao, received doting love unlike any of the other sons.
translations.idiomatic: As Consort Hui rose in favor, the mothers of Princes E and Guang were likewise pushed aside. Her son, Prince of Shou Mao, was doted on as none of the other princes were.

sentences.zh: 瑛於內第與鄂、光王等自謂母氏失職，嘗有怨望。

translations.literal: Ying, in the inner quarters with Princes of E and Guang and others, considered that their mothers had lost position and at times harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace, Ying and Princes E and Guang felt that their mothers had fallen from favor and sometimes gave voice to their grievances.

sentences.zh: 惠妃女咸宜公主出降於楊洄，洄希惠妃之旨，規利於己，日求其短，譖於惠妃。

translations.literal: Consort Hui's daughter, Princess Xianyi, was given in marriage to Yang Hui. Hui hoped to please Consort Hui and scheme for his own advantage; day by day he sought their faults and slandered them to Consort Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Hui's daughter, Princess Xianyi, married Yang Hui. Eager to curry favor with Consort Hui and advance his own interests, Hui daily hunted for faults in the princes and whispered accusations to the consort.

sentences.zh: 妃泣訴於玄宗，以太子結黨，將害於妾母子，亦指斥於至尊。

translations.literal: The consort wept and complained to Xuanzong that the crown prince was forming a faction and would harm her and her son, and also spoke reproaches against the sovereign himself.
translations.idiomatic: Weeping, she told Xuanzong that the crown prince was building a faction and plotting harm against her and her son, and even spoke against the emperor himself.

sentences.zh: 玄宗惑其言，震怒，謀於宰相，意將廢黜。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was swayed by her words, was shaken with rage, and took counsel with the chief ministers, intending to depose and dismiss them.
translations.idiomatic: Taken in by her account, Xuanzong flew into a rage and consulted his chief ministers with the intention of deposing the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 中書張九齡奏曰：「陛下纂嗣鴻業，將三十年，太子已下，常不離深宮，日受聖訓。

translations.literal: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling memorialized, saying: "Your Majesty has inherited and continued the great enterprise for nearly thirty years. From the crown prince downward, they have constantly not left the deep palace and daily received your sagely instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling submitted a memorial: "Your Majesty has carried on the great inheritance for nearly thirty years. From the crown prince down, your sons have scarcely left the inner palace and have received your instruction every day.

sentences.zh: 今天下之人，皆慶陛下享國日久，子孫蕃育，不聞有過，陛下奈何以一日之間廢棄三子？

translations.literal: Now all under heaven rejoice that Your Majesty has long enjoyed the state and that your sons and grandsons flourish and multiply; no fault has been heard of them—how can Your Majesty in a single day cast aside three sons?
translations.idiomatic: All the realm rejoices that you have long held the throne and that your sons flourish; no wrongdoing has been reported—how can you, in a single day, cast aside three of them?

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下思之。

translations.literal: I humbly beg Your Majesty to reflect on this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 且太子國本，難於動搖。

translations.literal: Moreover, the crown prince is the root of the state and is hard to move or shake.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the crown prince is the foundation of the state and must not be lightly disturbed.

sentences.zh: 昔晉獻公惑寵嬖之言，太子申生憂死，國乃大亂。

translations.literal: Formerly Duke Xian of Jin was misled by the words of a favored concubine; Crown Prince Shensheng died in grief, and the state fell into great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity Duke Xian of Jin was swayed by a favored woman's words; Crown Prince Shensheng died in despair, and the state was thrown into chaos.

sentences.zh: 漢武威加六合，受江充巫蠱之事，將禍及太子，遂至城中流血。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Han's martial might extended over the six directions, yet he accepted Jiang Chong's witchcraft affair; disaster was about to reach the crown prince, and blood flowed in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Han, whose might filled the realm, was taken in by Jiang Chong's witchcraft scandal; calamity nearly engulfed the heir, and blood ran in the capital streets.

sentences.zh: 晉惠帝有賢子為太子，容賈後之譖，以至喪亡。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy son as crown prince, yet tolerated Empress Jia's slanders, until he was lost and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin had a worthy heir, yet indulged Empress Jia's slanders until the dynasty itself was undone.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝取寵婦之言，廢太子勇而立晉王廣，遂失天下。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui took a favored woman's words, deposed Crown Prince Yong and installed Prince of Jin Guang, and thus lost the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui listened to a favored consort, deposed Crown Prince Yong in favor of Prince of Jin Guang, and in the end lost the empire.

sentences.zh: 由此而論之，不可不慎。

translations.literal: Judging from these examples, one cannot but be cautious.
translations.idiomatic: From these precedents, the matter cannot be treated lightly.

sentences.zh: 今太子既長無過，二王又賢，臣待罪左右，敢不詳悉。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince has grown up without fault, and the two princes are again worthy; your servant, holding office at your side, dares not fail to know this in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Today the crown prince has come of age without fault, and the two princes are worthy as well. Serving at Your Majesty's side, how could I fail to know this thoroughly?

sentences.zh: 」玄宗默然，事且寢。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong was silent, and the matter for the time being was laid to rest.
translations.idiomatic: " Xuanzong said nothing, and for the moment the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 其年，駕幸西京，以李林甫代張九齡為中書令，希惠妃之旨，托意於中貴人，揚壽王瑁之美，惠妃深德之。

translations.literal: That year, when the imperial carriage visited the Western Capital, Li Linfu replaced Zhang Jiuling as chief minister. Hoping to please Consort Hui's wishes, he conveyed his intent through the chief eunuchs and praised the excellence of Prince of Shou Mao; Consort Hui was deeply grateful.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the court moved to the Western Capital, Li Linfu replaced Zhang Jiuling as chief minister. Eager to please Consort Hui, he worked through the chief eunuchs to praise Prince of Shou Mao, and the consort was deeply obliged to him.

sentences.zh: 二十五年四月，楊洄又構於惠妃，言瑛兄弟三人與太子妃兄駙馬薛鏽常構異謀。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-fifth year, Yang Hui again framed charges before Consort Hui, saying that the three brothers Ying, Yao, and Ju, together with the crown prince's consort's brother, the imperial son-in-law Xue Xiu, often plotted strange designs.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiyuan 25, Yang Hui again laid accusations before Consort Hui, claiming that Ying and his two brothers, together with the crown prince's brother-in-law, Imperial Son-in-law Xue Xiu, were constantly plotting treason.

sentences.zh: 玄宗遽召宰相籌之，林甫曰：「此蓋陛下家事，臣不合參知。

translations.literal: Xuanzong hastily summoned the chief ministers to deliberate. Linfu said: "This is surely Your Majesty's household affair; your servant ought not to take part in knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong at once summoned the chief ministers to discuss the matter. Linfu said, "This is Your Majesty's family business; it is not for a subject to meddle in.

sentences.zh: 」玄宗意乃決矣。

translations.literal: " Xuanzong's mind was then decided.
translations.idiomatic: " With that, Xuanzong's mind was made up.

sentences.zh: 使中官宣詔於宮中，並廢為庶人，鏽配流，俄賜死於城東驛。

translations.literal: He sent eunuchs to proclaim the edict within the palace; all were deposed to commoner status. Xiu was sentenced to exile, and soon was granted death at the eastern suburb relay station.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs proclaimed the edict in the palace: all three princes were reduced to commoners. Xiu was banished and soon ordered to take his own life at the relay station east of the city.

sentences.zh: 天下之人不見其過，鹹惜之。

translations.literal: People throughout the realm had not seen their faults and all alike lamented them.
translations.idiomatic: The people had seen no fault in them, and all alike mourned their fall.

sentences.zh: 其年，武惠妃數見三庶人為崇，怖而成疾，巫者祈請彌月，不痊而殞。

translations.literal: That year, Consort Wu Hui repeatedly saw the three deposed men as malign spirits; terrified, she fell ill. Shamans prayed for a full month, but she did not recover and died.
translations.idiomatic: That same year Consort Wu Hui was repeatedly haunted by visions of the three deposed princes. Stricken with fear, she fell ill. Shamans prayed for a month, but she did not recover and died.

sentences.zh: 瑛有六男：儼、伸、倩、俅、備、亻敬。

translations.literal: Ying had six sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, Bei, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ying had six sons: Yan, Shen, Qian, Qiu, Bei, and Jing.

sentences.zh: 慶王琮先無子，瑛得罪後，玄宗遣鞫之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qing Cong had earlier had no sons; after Ying's offense, Xuanzong sent men to investigate and take them.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qing Cong had had no sons. After Ying's disgrace, Xuanzong had his sons investigated and assigned to Cong.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，儼為新平郡王、光祿卿同正員，伸為平原郡王、宗正卿同正員，俅為嗣慶王。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era, Yan was made Prince of Xinping commandery and acting regular commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Shen was made Prince of Pingyuan commandery and acting director of the Imperial Clan Court; Qiu was made heir to Prince of Qing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao period Yan was created Prince of Xinping and given acting rank as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Shen was made Prince of Pingyuan and acting director of the Imperial Clan Court; Qiu was named heir to Prince of Qing.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，詔雪瑤、瑛、琚之罪，贈瑛為皇太子，瑤、琚復贈為王。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying, an edict cleared the crimes of Yao, Ying, and Ju; Ying was posthumously given the title of crown prince, and Yao and Ju were again posthumously enfeoffed as princes.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 (762) an edict cleared the charges against Yao, Ying, and Ju. Ying was posthumously restored as crown prince, and Yao and Ju were again granted princely titles.

sentences.zh: 棣王琰，玄宗第四子也，初名嗣真。

translations.literal: Prince of Di Yan was Emperor Xuanzong's fourth son; his original name was Sizhen.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Di Yan was Xuanzong's fourth son; his birth name was Sizhen.

sentences.zh: 開元二年十二月，封為鄫王。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Kaiyuan 2 (714) he was created Prince of Zeng.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，改封棣王，仍改名洽。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, he was re-enfeoffed as Prince of Di and at the same time renamed Qia.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 12 he was re-created Prince of Di and renamed Qia.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領太原牧、太原已北諸軍節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the governorship of Taiyuan and the post of military commissioner of all armies north of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was given nominal command as governor of Taiyuan and military commissioner of all forces north of that city.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，加太子太傅，余如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, he was additionally made grand preceptor of the heir apparent; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 22 he was additionally appointed grand preceptor of the heir apparent while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，改名琰。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Yan.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年六月，遙領兼武威郡都督、河西隴右經略節度大使。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao, he additionally held in title the governorship of Wuwei commandery and the post of frontier commissioner of Hexi and Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianbao 1 (742) he was also given nominal rank as governor of Wuwei and frontier commissioner of Hexi and Longyou.

sentences.zh: 先是，琰妃韋氏有過，琰怒之，不敢奏聞，乃斥於別室。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yan's consort of the Wei clan had committed an offense; Yan was angry with her but did not dare report it and instead confined her to a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Yan's consort, of the Wei clan, had given offense. Angry but unwilling to report the matter, he shut her away in a separate apartment.

sentences.zh: 寵二孺人，孺人又不相協。

translations.literal: He favored two ladies of lower rank, and the ladies in turn did not get along with each other.
translations.idiomatic: He favored two junior consorts, who were also at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 至十一載，孺人乃密求巫者，書符置於琰履中以求媚。

translations.literal: By the eleventh year, one of the ladies secretly sought a shaman, who wrote a talisman and placed it in Yan's shoe to win favor.
translations.idiomatic: By Tianbao 11 one of the junior consorts secretly hired a shaman to write a charm and slip it into Yan's shoe, hoping to win his affection.

sentences.zh: 琰與監院中官有隙，中官聞其事，密奏於玄宗，雲琰厭魅聖躬。

translations.literal: Yan had a rift with a eunuch superintendent of the residence; the eunuch heard of the affair and secretly memorialized Xuanzong, saying that Yan was using sorcery to harm the sacred person.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had quarreled with a eunuch who supervised his household. Learning of the charm, the eunuch secretly reported to Xuanzong that Yan was practicing witchcraft against the emperor.

sentences.zh: 玄宗使人掩其履而獲之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong sent men to seize his shoe and obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong had men search Yan's shoes and found the talisman.

sentences.zh: 玄宗大怒，引琰詰責之。

translations.literal: Xuanzong was greatly enraged, summoned Yan, and interrogated and rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong flew into a rage, summoned Yan, and sharply questioned him.

sentences.zh: 琰頓首謝曰：「臣之罪合死矣，請一言以就鼎鑊。

translations.literal: Yan bowed his head and apologized, saying: "Your servant's crime deserves death; I beg one word before I go to the cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Yan kowtowed and said, "I deserve death. Allow me one word before I face execution.

sentences.zh: 然臣與新婦，情義絕者，二年於茲，臣有二孺人，又皆爭長。

translations.literal: Yet between your servant and my new wife, affection has been severed for two years now; your servant has two ladies of lower rank, and both again vie for precedence.
translations.idiomatic: My wife and I have been estranged for two years. I have two junior consorts, and they too are constantly quarreling.

sentences.zh: 臣實不知有符，恐此三人所為也。

translations.literal: Your servant truly did not know of the talisman; I fear these three women did it.
translations.idiomatic: I truly knew nothing of the charm; I fear all three women are behind it.

sentences.zh: 惟三哥辯其罪人。

translations.literal: I ask only that the third brother identify the guilty person.
translations.idiomatic: Let the third brother determine which of them is guilty.

sentences.zh: 」及推問之，竟孺人也。

translations.literal: " When the matter was pressed in inquiry, in the end it was one of the ladies of lower rank.
translations.idiomatic: " Under questioning, it turned out to have been one of the junior consorts.

sentences.zh: 玄宗猶疑琰知情，怒未解，太子已下皆為請，命囚於鷹狗坊中，絕朝請，憂懼而死。

translations.literal: Xuanzong still suspected that Yan knew of it; his anger was not dispelled. From the crown prince downward all pleaded on his behalf, but he ordered Yan imprisoned in the Hawk and Hound Ward, cut off from court attendance, and Yan died in worry and fear.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong still suspected Yan had known of the plot, and his anger did not abate. The crown prince and the other princes all interceded, but the emperor had Yan confined in the Hawk and Hound Ward, barred from court, where he died of grief and fear.

sentences.zh: 琰妃即少師韋滔女，無子，琰死後，妃得還其父。

translations.literal: Yan's consort was the daughter of Junior Preceptor Wei Tao; she had no sons. After Yan's death, the consort was able to return to her father.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's consort was a daughter of Junior Preceptor Wei Tao. Childless, she was sent back to her father's house after Yan's death.

sentences.zh: 琰男女繁衍，至五十五人。

translations.literal: Yan's sons and daughters multiplied, reaching fifty-five in all.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's sons and daughters were numerous, reaching fifty-five in all.

sentences.zh: 天寶中封為王者三人：僎為汝南郡王、秘書監同正員，僑為宜都王、衛尉卿同正員，雋為濟南王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era three were enfeoffed as princes: Fu as Prince of Runan commandery and acting director of the Secretariat; Qiao as Prince of Yidu and acting minister of the Guards; Jun as Prince of Jinan and acting commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao three of his sons were created princes: Fu as Prince of Runan with acting rank as director of the Secretariat; Qiao as Prince of Yidu with acting rank as minister of the Guards; Jun as Prince of Jinan with acting rank as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月，代宗即位，舍琰罪，贈其王位。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, when Daizong took the throne, Yan's crime was set aside and his princely title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Baoying 1, when Daizong ascended the throne, Yan's conviction was set aside and his princely title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 鄂王瑤，玄宗第五子也，初名嗣初。

translations.literal: Prince of E Yao was Emperor Xuanzong's fifth son; his original name was Sichu.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of E Yao was Xuanzong's fifth son; his birth name was Sichu.

sentences.zh: 開元二年五月，封為鄂王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of E.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 2 he was created Prince of E.

sentences.zh: 十二年，改名涓，遙領幽州都督、河北道節度大使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, he was renamed Juan and held in title the governorship of Youzhou and the post of military commissioner of the Hebei circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 12 he was renamed Juan and given nominal command as governor of Youzhou and military commissioner of the Hebei circuit.

sentences.zh: 二十一年四月，加太子太保，兼幽州都督，余如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the twenty-first year, he was additionally made grand guardian of the heir apparent and concurrently governor of Youzhou; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Kaiyuan 21 he was additionally appointed grand guardian of the heir apparent while retaining his post as governor of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，改名瑤。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was renamed Yao.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was renamed Yao.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，得罪廢。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he offended and was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 he fell from favor and was deposed.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年五月追復。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Baoying, his title was posthumously restored.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Baoying 1 his title was posthumously restored.

sentences.zh: 靖恭太子琬，玄宗第六子也，初名嗣玄。

translations.literal: The Jinggong Heir Apparent Wan was Emperor Xuanzong's sixth son; his original name was Sixuan.
translations.idiomatic: The Jinggong Heir Apparent Wan was Xuanzong's sixth son; his birth name was Sixuan.

sentences.zh: 開元二年三月，封為甄王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 2 he was created Prince of Zhen.

sentences.zh: 十二年三月，改名滉，封為榮王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twelfth year, he was renamed Huang and re-enfeoffed as Prince of Rong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 12 he was renamed Huang and re-created Prince of Rong.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授京兆牧，又遙領隴右節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed governor of Jingzhao and additionally held in title the post of military commissioner of Longyou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was appointed governor of the capital district and given nominal command as military commissioner of Longyou.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，余如故。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was additionally given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office; his other posts remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was additionally granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff while retaining his other titles.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，改名琬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, he was renamed Wan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 he was renamed Wan.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年六月，授單於大都護。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the first year of Tianbao, he was appointed protector-general of Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianbao 1 he was appointed protector-general of Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 十四年十一月，安祿山反於范陽，其月制以琬為征討元帥，高仙芝為副，令仙芝征河、隴兵募屯於陜郡以禦之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang. That same month an edict made Wan commander-in-chief for the punitive campaign, with Gao Xianzhi as deputy, and ordered Xianzhi to levy troops from He and Long and encamp them in Shaan commandery to resist.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianbao 14 An Lushan rose in rebellion at Fanyang. That month Wan was named commander-in-chief of the punitive force, with Gao Xianzhi as his deputy, and Xianzhi was ordered to raise troops from the He and Long regions and station them in Shaan to meet the rebels.

sentences.zh: 數日，琬薨。

translations.literal: Within a few days, Wan died.
translations.idiomatic: A few days later Wan died.

sentences.zh: 琬素有雅稱，風格秀整，時士庶冀琬有所成功，忽然殂謝，遠近鹹失望焉。

translations.literal: Wan had long borne a refined reputation; his bearing was elegant and composed. At the time scholars and commoners alike hoped Wan would achieve success, but he suddenly passed away, and near and far all alike were disappointed.
translations.idiomatic: Wan had long enjoyed a reputation for refinement and carried himself with grace. Scholars and commoners alike had hoped he would distinguish himself in the campaign; his sudden death left the realm deeply disappointed.

sentences.zh: 贈靖恭太子，葬於見子西原。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given the title Jinggong Heir Apparent and buried on the western plain of Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as the Jinggong Heir Apparent and buried on the western plain at Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 琬諸子尤繁衍，男女五十八人。

translations.literal: Wan's sons and daughters were especially numerous, fifty-eight sons and daughters in all.
translations.idiomatic: Wan's offspring were especially numerous: fifty-eight sons and daughters in all.

sentences.zh: 天寶中封為郡王者二：俯為濟陰王、太仆卿同正員，偕為北平王、國子祭酒同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era two were enfeoffed as commandery princes: Fu as Prince of Jiyin and acting minister of the Stud; Xie as Prince of Beiping and acting chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao two of his sons were created commandery princes: Fu as Prince of Jiyin with acting rank as minister of the Stud; Xie as Prince of Beiping with acting rank as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 夏悼王一，玄宗第九子也。

translations.literal: Prince Xia Ci Yi was Emperor Xuanzong's ninth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xia Ci Yi was Xuanzong's ninth son.

sentences.zh: 母貞順皇后為惠妃，見寵。

translations.literal: His mother, Empress Zhenshun, had been Consort Hui and was favored.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, later Empress Zhenshun, had been Consort Wu Hui and was greatly favored.

sentences.zh: 一生而美秀，上鐘愛無比，名之為一。

translations.literal: From birth he was beautiful and refined; the emperor doted on him beyond compare and named him Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome from birth, he was doted on as no other child had been, and the emperor gave him the name Yi.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，孩孺而薨，玄宗追封謚。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaiyuan, while still an infant he died; Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed him and gave a posthumous title.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 he died in infancy, and Xuanzong posthumously enfeoffed him and granted a posthumous title.

sentences.zh: 時車駕在東都，葬於城南龍門東岑，欲宮中舉目見之。

translations.literal: At the time the imperial carriage was in the Eastern Capital; he was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen south of the city, so that the palace might see it at a glance.
translations.idiomatic: The court was then at the Eastern Capital. He was buried on the eastern slope of Longmen south of the city, placed so that the palace could see the tomb from afar.

sentences.zh: 儀王璲，玄宗第十二子也，初名濰。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Lin was Emperor Xuanzong's twelfth son; his original name was Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi Lin was Xuanzong's twelfth son; his birth name was Wei.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年五月，封為儀王。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，授河南牧。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he was appointed governor of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was appointed governor of Henan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，兼河南牧，其年改名璲。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was additionally given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and concurrently held the governorship of Henan; that year he was renamed Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff while retaining the governorship of Henan, and that year he was renamed Lin.

sentences.zh: 永泰元年二月薨，廢朝三日，贈太傅。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Yongtai, he died; court was suspended for three days, and he was posthumously made grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of Yongtai 1 (765). Court mourning was observed for three days, and he was posthumously honored as grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 天寶中有子封王者二人：侁為鐘陵郡王、光祿卿同正員，僆為廣陵王、國子祭酒同正員。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Shen as Prince of Zhongling commandery and acting commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Mian as Prince of Guangling and acting chancellor of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Shen as Prince of Zhongling with acting rank as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; Mian as Prince of Guangling with acting rank as chancellor of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 潁王璬，玄宗第十三子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Ying Li was Emperor Xuanzong's thirteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ying Li was Xuanzong's thirteenth son.

sentences.zh: 讀書有文詞。

translations.literal: In his studies he had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: He was learned and wrote with literary grace.

sentences.zh: 初名澐。

translations.literal: His original name was Yun.
translations.idiomatic: His birth name was Yun.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，封潁王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Ying.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領安東都護、平盧軍節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the protectorship of Andong and the post of military commissioner of the Pinglu army.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was given nominal command as protector of Andong and military commissioner of the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，改名璬。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, he was additionally given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and was renamed Li.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff and was renamed Li.

sentences.zh: 安祿山反，除蜀郡大都督、劍南節度大使，楊國忠為之副。

translations.literal: When An Lushan rebelled, Li was appointed grand governor of Shu commandery and military commissioner of Jiannan, with Yang Guozhong as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When An Lushan rose in rebellion, Li was appointed grand governor of Shu and military commissioner of Jiannan, with Yang Guozhong as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 玄宗幸蜀，令御史大夫魏方進充置頓使，先移牒至蜀，托以潁王之籓，令設儲供。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong fled to Shu, he ordered Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin to serve as commissioner for arranging halting-stations, and first sent a dispatch ahead to Shu in the name of Prince Ying's journey to his fief, instructing that stores and supplies be prepared.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong fled to Shu, he appointed Censor-in-Chief Wei Fangjin commissioner for lodging along the route and sent a dispatch ahead to Shu in the name of Prince Ying's departure for his fief, instructing the province to prepare provisions and supplies.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至馬嵬，方進被殺，乃令璬先赴本郡，以蜀郡長史崔圓為副。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong reached Mawei, Fangjin was killed; he then ordered Li to go first to his own commandery, with Cui Yuan, chief administrator of Shu, as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: At Mawei, Fangjin was killed. The emperor then ordered Li to proceed at once to his commandery and appointed Cui Yuan, chief administrator of Shu, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 璬性儉率，將渡綿州江，登舟見彩緣席為藉者，顧曰：「此可以為寢處，奈何踐之？

translations.literal: Li was by nature frugal and unadorned. As he was about to cross the river at Mianzhou, he boarded a boat and saw colored-edged mats laid down as foot coverings. He turned and said, "These could serve as bedding—how can we tread upon them?
translations.idiomatic: Frugal and plain by temperament, Li was about to cross the Mianzhou River when, upon boarding, he noticed colored-edged mats spread underfoot. He looked back and said, "These could be used for sleeping—why should we trample them?

sentences.zh: 」命撤去。

translations.literal: " He ordered them removed.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered the mats taken away.

sentences.zh: 璬初奉命之籓，卒遽不遑受節，綿州司馬史賁進說曰：「王，帝子也，且為節度大使。

translations.literal: When Li first received orders to go to his fief, in the end he was in such haste that he had no time to receive the commissioner's insignia. Shi Benjin, vice-administrator of Mianzhou, urged him, saying, "Your Highness is the emperor's son, and moreover a military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li had set out on imperial orders for his fief before he could receive the commissioner's insignia of office. Shi Benjin, vice-administrator of Mianzhou, pressed him, saying, "Your Highness is the emperor's own son—and a military commissioner besides.

sentences.zh: 今之籓而不持節，單騎徑進，人何所贍？

translations.literal: Now you go to your fief without holding insignia, advancing alone on horseback—what will people look to?
translations.idiomatic: If you enter your domain without insignia and ride ahead alone, what authority will the people recognize in you?

sentences.zh: 請建大槊，蒙之油囊，為旌節狀，先驅道路，足以威眾。

translations.literal: Please erect a great spear, cover it with an oiled leather sleeve, make it in the form of banners and insignia, and send it ahead to clear the road—it will be enough to awe the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Let us raise a great spear, wrap it in an oiled leather case, and shape it like the banners and baton of command to march at the fore. That alone would be enough to overawe the crowd.

sentences.zh: 」璬笑曰：「但為真王，何用假旌節乎？

translations.literal: " Li smiled and said, "If one is a true prince, what need is there for false banners and insignia?
translations.idiomatic: " Li smiled and said, "A true prince has no need of counterfeit insignia.

sentences.zh: 」將至成都，崔圓迓之，拜於馬前，璬不止之，圓頗怒。

translations.literal: " As they were about to reach Chengdu, Cui Yuan came out to meet him and bowed before his horse; Li did not immediately bid him rise, and Yuan was greatly displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " Near Chengdu, Cui Yuan came forward to welcome him and prostrated himself before the horse. Li did not promptly tell him to rise, and Yuan took deep offense.

sentences.zh: 玄宗至，璬視事兩月，人甚安之。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong arrived, Li administered affairs for two months, and the people were very much at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuanzong's arrival, Li governed for two months, and the people found the region greatly settled.

sentences.zh: 為圓所奏，罷居內宅。

translations.literal: Memorialized against by Yuan, he was dismissed and made to reside in the inner residence.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yuan memorialized against him, and he was removed from office to live in the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 後令宣慰肅宗於彭原，遂從歸京師。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to go to Pengyuan to convey comfort to Emperor Suzong, and thereafter followed him back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was later sent to Pengyuan to pay respects and offer reassurance to Emperor Suzong, then accompanied the court back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建中四年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth year of the Jianzhong era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Jianzhong.

sentences.zh: 年六十六，輟朝三日。

translations.literal: He was sixty-six years old; court audiences were suspended for three days.
translations.idiomatic: He was sixty-six. The court mourned him with a three-day suspension of audiences.

sentences.zh: 子伸，天寶中封滎陽郡王，授衛尉卿同正員。

translations.literal: His son Shen, during the Tianbao era, was enfeoffed as Prince of Xingyang commandery and appointed acting regular minister of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen was enfeoffed as Prince of Xingyang during the Tianbao reign and appointed acting minister of the Guards with full rank.

sentences.zh: 懷哀王敏，玄宗第十五子也。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'ai Min was Emperor Xuanzong's fifteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai'ai Min was Xuanzong's fifteenth son.

sentences.zh: 幼而豐秀，以母惠妃之寵，玄宗特加顧念。

translations.literal: From childhood he was plump and handsome; because of his mother Consort Wu Hui's favor, Xuanzong paid him special regard.
translations.idiomatic: Handsome and robust from boyhood, he won extraordinary attention from Xuanzong on account of his mother, Consort Wu Hui, whom the emperor favored.

sentences.zh: 才晬，開元八年二月薨，追封謚，權窆於景龍觀。

translations.literal: Having barely reached his first birthday, he died in the second month of the eighth year of Kaiyuan; posthumous enfeoffment and a title were granted, and he was provisionally interred at Jinglong Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of Kaiyuan 8, not yet two years old. The court granted him posthumous rank and a title and temporarily buried him at Jinglong Abbey.

sentences.zh: 天寶十三載，改葬京城南，以祔其母敬陵也。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianbao, he was reinterred south of the capital to be appended to the tomb of his mother, Jingling.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 13 he was reburied south of the capital and laid to rest beside his mother in Jingling.

sentences.zh: 永王璘，玄宗第十六子也。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Lin was Emperor Xuanzong's sixteenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Lin was Xuanzong's sixteenth son.

sentences.zh: 母曰郭順儀，劍南節度尚書虛己之妹。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Guo the Honored Consort, younger sister of Xu Ji, minister in charge of the Jiannan circuit.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Honored Consort Guo, sister of Xu Ji, who served as minister overseeing the Jiannan circuit.

sentences.zh: 璘數歲失母，肅宗收養，夜自抱眠之。

translations.literal: Lin lost his mother at several years of age; Suzong took him in and raised him, at night holding him in his own arms to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Lin lost his mother while still a small child. Suzong took him in and reared him, cradling him in his own arms at night until he slept.

sentences.zh: 少聰敏好學，貌陋，視物不正。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and eager to learn; his appearance was homely, and he did not look straight at things.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy he was bright and studious, though plain in appearance and with a wandering, unfocused gaze.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為永王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince Yong.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，遙領荊州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fifteenth year, he held in title the post of grand governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Kaiyuan 15 he was named grand governor of Jingzhou in absentia.

sentences.zh: 二十年七月，加開府儀同三司，改名璘。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twentieth year, he was additionally given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and was renamed Lin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 20 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff and was renamed Lin.

sentences.zh: 天寶十四載十一月，安祿山反范陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourteenth year of Tianbao, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Tianbao 14, An Lushan rebelled at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 十五載六月，玄宗幸蜀，至漢中郡，下詔以璘為山南東路及嶺南黔中江南西路四道節度采訪等使、江陵郡大都督，余如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year, Xuanzong fled to Shu; when he reached Hanzhong commandery, he issued an edict appointing Lin commissioner of pacification and inspection over the four circuits of Shannan East Route, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West Route, and grand governor of Jiangling commandery, with his other titles remaining as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianbao 15, Xuanzong fled to Shu. At Hanzhong he issued an edict making Lin commissioner of pacification and inspection over Shannan East, Lingnan, Qianzhong, and Jiangnan West, and grand governor of Jiangling, while his existing honors remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 璘七月至襄陽，九月至江陵，召募士將數萬人，恣情補署，江淮租賦，山積於江陵，破用鉅億。

translations.literal: Lin reached Xiangyang in the seventh month and Jiangling in the ninth month, recruiting officers and soldiers numbering in the tens of thousands; he appointed people at will; the tax revenues of the Jianghuai region piled up at Jiangling like mountains, and expenditures ran to hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Lin arrived at Xiangyang in the seventh month and Jiangling in the ninth, where he recruited tens of thousands of officers and men and handed out appointments as he pleased. Jianghuai tax grain stacked up at Jiangling like hills, and his spending ran into the hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 以薛镠、李臺卿、蔡坰為謀主，因有異志。

translations.literal: Taking Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, and Cai Jiong as his chief strategists, he thus harbored rebellious intentions.
translations.idiomatic: With Xue Liu, Li Taiqing, and Cai Jiong as his principal advisers, he began to nourish designs of rebellion.

sentences.zh: 肅宗聞之，詔令歸覲於蜀，璘不從命。

translations.literal: When Suzong heard of this, he ordered Lin to return to Shu to pay homage; Lin did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, hearing of this, ordered Lin to come to Shu and render homage. Lin refused.

sentences.zh: 十二月，擅領舟師東下，甲仗五千人趨廣陵，以季廣琛、渾惟明、高仙琦為將。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on his own authority he led a fleet eastward downriver, five thousand men in armor and arms rushing toward Guangling, with Ji Guangchen, Hun Weiming, and Gao Xianqi as his generals.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he took it upon himself to lead a river fleet eastward, five thousand armed men hurrying toward Guangling under the generals Ji Guangchen, Hun Weiming, and Gao Xianqi.

sentences.zh: 璘生於宮中，不更人事，其子襄城王亻易又勇而有力，馭兵權，為左右眩惑，遂謀狂悖。

translations.literal: Lin had been born in the palace and had no experience of worldly affairs; his son the Prince of Xiangcheng, Yi, was moreover brave and strong, wielded military authority, and was deluded by those around him, whereupon they plotted outrageous treason.
translations.idiomatic: Raised entirely within the palace, Lin knew nothing of the world outside. His son, Prince Yi of Xiangcheng, was bold and powerful, held the reins of the army, and was swayed by flatterers until together they embarked on a mad and treasonous course.

sentences.zh: 璘雖有窺江左之心，而未露其事。

translations.literal: Although Lin harbored designs on the lands east of the Yangtze, he had not yet revealed his plans.
translations.idiomatic: Lin already coveted the lower Yangtze region, though he had not yet shown his hand.

sentences.zh: 吳郡采訪使李希言乃平牒璘，大署其名，璘遂激怒，牒報曰：「寡人上皇天屬，皇帝友於，地尊侯王，禮絕僚品，簡書來往，應有常儀，今乃平牒抗威，落筆署字，漢儀隳紊，一至於斯！

translations.literal: Li Xiyan, Pacification and Inspection Commissioner of Wu Commandery, sent Lin a dispatch on equal footing and signed his name in large characters. Lin was enraged and replied by dispatch: "I am the Heaven-appointed kin of the Retired Emperor, the emperor's brother in affection, exalted in rank as a prince, and set apart in ritual from the ranks of officials. Correspondence between us ought to observe fixed forms. Yet now you send a dispatch of equal rank to flaunt your authority, signing your name with a stroke of the brush—Han ritual overthrown and disordered, to such a point as this!
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiyan, pacification commissioner of Wu Commandery, addressed Lin in a dispatch of equal rank and signed his name in bold, oversized characters. Lin flew into a rage and answered: "I am kin to the Retired Emperor by Heaven's mandate, the reigning emperor's own brother; in station I stand above every noble rank, and protocol places me beyond the company of officials. Letters between us should follow fixed forms. Yet you now send a dispatch on equal terms to affront my authority, scrawling your signature in outsized hand. The rites of the Han court are thrown into chaos—even to this!"

sentences.zh: 」乃使渾惟明取希言，季廣琛趣廣陵攻采訪李成式。

translations.literal: " He then sent Hun Weiming to seize Xiyan, and Ji Guangchen to hurry to Guangling and attack Pacification Commissioner Li Chengshi.
translations.idiomatic: " He then dispatched Hun Weiming to capture Xiyan and Ji Guangchen to strike Guangling and attack the pacification commissioner Li Chengshi.

sentences.zh: 璘進至當塗，希言在丹陽，令元景曜、閻敬之等以兵拒之，身走吳郡，李成式使將李承慶拒之。

translations.literal: Lin advanced to Dangtu. Xiyan was at Danyang and ordered Yuan Jingyao, Yan Jingzhi, and others to resist with troops; he himself fled to Wu Commandery, while Li Chengshi sent the general Li Chengqing to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Lin pushed forward to Dangtu. Xiyan, at Danyang, ordered Yuan Jingyao, Yan Jingzhi, and others to hold him off with troops, then fled in person to Wu Commandery. Li Chengshi sent his general Li Chengqing to meet the advance.

sentences.zh: 先是，肅宗以璘不受命，先使中官啖廷瑤、段喬福招討之。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Lin would not accept orders, Suzong had first sent the eunuchs Dan Tingyao and Duan Qiaofu to raise troops against him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Lin refused to obey, Suzong had already sent the eunuchs Dan Tingyao and Duan Qiaofu to subdue him by force or persuasion.

sentences.zh: 中官至廣陵，反式括得馬數百匹。

translations.literal: When the eunuchs reached Guangling, they were instead requisitioned by Li Chengshi and obtained several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: By the time the eunuchs reached Guangling, Li Chengshi had already impressed them into service and seized several hundred horses from them.

sentences.zh: 時河北招討判官、司虞郎中李銑在廣陵，瑤等結銑為兄弟，求之將兵。

translations.literal: At that time Li Xian, adjutant of the Hebei pacification force and director in the Ministry of Justice, was at Guangling; Tingyao and the others swore brotherhood with Xian and asked him to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian, adjutant on the Hebei pacification staff and a director in the Ministry of Justice, was then at Guangling. Tingyao and his party bound themselves to Xian in sworn brotherhood and begged him to take command.

sentences.zh: 銑麾下有騎一百八十人，遂率所領屯於楊子，成式使判官評事裴茂以廣陵步卒三千同拒於瓜步洲伊婁埭。

translations.literal: Under Xian's command were one hundred eighty horsemen; he then led his force and encamped at Yangzi; Chengshi sent the judge-assessor Pei Mao with three thousand infantry from Guangling to join in resisting at Yilou Dam on Guabu Isle in the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had one hundred eighty cavalry under him. He marched them to camp at Yangzi, while Chengshi sent the judge Pei Mao with three thousand Guangling foot soldiers to block the route together at Yilou Dam on Guabu Isle.

sentences.zh: 希言將元景曜及成式將李神慶並以其眾迎降於璘，璘又殺丹徒太守閻敬之以徇。

translations.literal: Xiyan's general Yuan Jingyao and Chengshi's general Li Shenqing both led their forces in surrender to Lin; Lin also executed Yan Jingzhi, prefect of Dantu, as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jingyao, Xiyan's commander, and Li Shenqing, Chengshi's commander, both brought their men over to Lin. Lin also put Yan Jingzhi, prefect of Dantu, to death as a public warning.

sentences.zh: 江左大駭。

translations.literal: The lands east of the Yangtze were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: All the lands south of the Yangtze were thrown into terror.

sentences.zh: 裴茂至瓜步洲，廣張旗幟，耀於江津。

translations.literal: Pei Mao reached Guabu Isle, spread banners wide, and displayed them brilliantly on the river crossing.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Mao came to Guabu Isle, unfurled a forest of banners, and blazed with color along the river crossing.

sentences.zh: 璘與亻易登陴望之竟日，始有懼色。

translations.literal: Lin and Yi climbed the wall and gazed at them all day before fear finally showed on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Yi mounted the ramparts and watched all day long before dread at last crept into their faces.

sentences.zh: 季廣琛召諸將割臂而盟，以貳於璘。

translations.literal: Ji Guangchen summoned the generals, cut their arms, and swore an oath, thereby turning against Lin.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Guangchen called the generals together, cut their arms in a blood oath, and broke with Lin.

sentences.zh: 是日，渾惟明走於江寧，馮季康、康謙投於廣陵之白沙。

translations.literal: That day Hun Weiming fled to Jiangning, and Feng Jikang and Kang Qian surrendered at Baisha in Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Hun Weiming fled to Jiangning, while Feng Jikang and Kang Qian gave themselves up at Baisha near Guangling.

sentences.zh: 廣琛以步卒六千趨廣陵，璘使騎追之，廣琛曰：「我感王恩，是以不能決戰，逃而歸國。

translations.literal: Guangchen led six thousand infantry toward Guangling; Lin sent cavalry in pursuit, and Guangchen said: "I am moved by the prince's grace, and therefore cannot bring myself to fight a decisive battle; I flee to return to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchen marched six thousand foot soldiers toward Guangling; Lin sent horsemen after him, and Guangchen said, "Out of gratitude to Your Highness I cannot bring myself to meet you in battle; I am leaving to return to the emperor's service.

sentences.zh: 若逼我，我則不擇地而回戰矣。

translations.literal: If you press me, I shall fight you back without choosing the ground.
translations.idiomatic: But if you drive me to it, I will turn and fight wherever I stand.

sentences.zh: 」使者返報。

translations.literal: The messenger returned and reported this.
translations.idiomatic: The messenger came back with his answer.

sentences.zh: 其夕，銑等多燃火，人執兩炬以疑之，隔江望者，兼水中之影，一皆為二矣。

translations.literal: That evening Xian and the others lit many fires; each man held two torches to create doubt; those watching from across the river, together with the reflections in the water, saw everything doubled.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xian's men lit fires all along the bank, each soldier carrying two torches to confuse the eye; watchers on the far shore, and the river mirroring the flames, saw every light become two.

sentences.zh: 璘軍又以火應之。

translations.literal: Lin's army also answered with fire.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's army answered with fires of their own.

sentences.zh: 璘懼，以官軍悉濟矣，遂以兒女及麾下宵遁。

translations.literal: Lin feared that the government army had all crossed over, and so fled by night with his children and followers.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, believing the whole imperial host had crossed the river, fled in the dark with his family and retainers.

sentences.zh: 遲明，不見濟者，遂入城具舟楫，使襄城王驅其眾以奔晉陵。

translations.literal: At dawn, seeing no one crossing, he entered the city, prepared boats, and sent the Prince of Xiangcheng to drive the army in flight toward Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: When dawn showed no crossing at all, he entered the city, gathered boats, and ordered the Prince of Xiangcheng to whip the army toward Jinling.

sentences.zh: 宵諜曰：「王走矣。

translations.literal: A night scout said: "The prince has fled."
translations.idiomatic: A scout in the night cried, "The prince is gone!"

sentences.zh: 」於是江北之軍齊進，募敢死士趙侃、庫狄岫、趙連城等共二十人，先鋒遊弈於新豐，皆因醉而寐。

translations.literal: Thereupon the army north of the river advanced together; they recruited dare-to-die men—Zhao Kan, Kudie Xiu, Zhao Liancheng, and twenty others in all—who as vanguard ranged ahead at Xinfeng, and all fell drunk asleep.
translations.idiomatic: Then the northern army moved as one; they enlisted dare-to-die men—Zhao Kan, Kudie Xiu, Zhao Liancheng, and twenty others—who rode ahead as scouts to Xinfeng and there, drunk, slept.

sentences.zh: 璘聞官軍之至，乃使襄城王、高仙琦逆擊之。

translations.literal: When Lin heard that the government army had arrived, he sent the Prince of Xiangcheng and Gao Xianqi to strike them in counterattack.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the imperial force was near, Lin sent the Prince of Xiangcheng and Gao Xianqi to meet it head on.

sentences.zh: 驛騎奔告，侃等介馬而出，襄城王已隨而至，銑等奔救，張左右翼擊之，射中襄城王首，亻易軍遂敗。

translations.literal: Post riders came galloping with the report; Kan and the others mounted in armor and sallied forth; the Prince of Xiangcheng was already upon them; Xian and the others raced to the rescue, spread left and right wings, and struck; an arrow struck the Prince of Xiangcheng in the head, and Yi's army was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Courier horses thundered in with word of attack; Kan and his men armored up and rode out—but the Prince of Xiangcheng was already on them. Xian rushed to their aid, split his wings, and closed; an arrow took the prince in the head, and Yi's force broke.

sentences.zh: 高仙琦等四騎與璘南奔，至鄱陽郡，司馬陶備閉城拒之。

translations.literal: Gao Xianqi and four other horsemen fled south with Lin to Poyang commandery; the vice prefect Tao Bei closed the city and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xianqi and four riders fled south with Lin as far as Poyang, where Vice Prefect Tao Bei shut the gates against them.

sentences.zh: 璘怒，命焚其城。

translations.literal: Lin was enraged and ordered the city burned.
translations.idiomatic: Lin in his rage commanded the city put to the torch.

sentences.zh: 至余幹，及大庾嶺，將南投嶺外，為江西采訪使皇甫侁下防禦兵所擒，因中矢而薨。

translations.literal: When he reached Yugan and the Dayu Range, as he was about to flee south beyond the mountains, he was captured by the defensive troops under Huangfu Shen, inspection commissioner of Jiangxi, and died from an arrow wound.
translations.idiomatic: At Yugan and the Dayu Pass, as he sought refuge beyond the southern ranges, the Jiangxi inspection commissioner Huangfu Shen's garrison took him; he died of an arrow wound.

sentences.zh: 子亻易等為亂兵所害。

translations.literal: His son Yi and others were killed by the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yi and the rest were cut down by the disorderly troops.

sentences.zh: 肅宗以璘愛弟，隱而不言。

translations.literal: Because Suzong had loved Lin as a younger brother, he concealed the matter and did not speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong, loving Lin as a brother, kept silent and would not speak openly of what had passed.

sentences.zh: 壽王瑁，玄宗第十八子也，初名清。

translations.literal: Prince of Shou Mao was Emperor Xuanzong's eighteenth son; his original name was Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Shou Mao was Xuanzong's eighteenth son; his birth name was Qing.

sentences.zh: 初，瑁母武惠妃，開元元年見幸，寵傾後宮，頻產夏悼王、懷哀王、上仙公主，皆端麗，繈褓不育。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mao's mother Consort Wu Hui, in the first year of Kaiyuan, received the emperor's favor; her favor overturned the rear palace; she frequently bore Prince Xia Ci, Prince Huai'ai, and Princess Shangxian—all comely—and none survived swaddling clothes.
translations.idiomatic: At first Mao's mother, Consort Wu Hui, won the emperor's favor in Kaiyuan 1 and eclipsed every woman in the inner quarters; she bore Prince Xia Ci, Prince Huai'ai, and Princess Shangxian, each fair of face, yet none lived beyond infancy.

sentences.zh: 及瑁之初生，讓帝妃元氏請瑁在於邸中收養，妃自乳之，名為己子。

translations.literal: When Mao was first born, Consort Yuan of the Abdicated Emperor asked to raise Mao in her residence; the consort herself nursed him and called him her own son.
translations.idiomatic: When Mao was born, Consort Yuan of the Prince of Rang asked to raise him in her household; she suckled him herself and named him as her own.

sentences.zh: 十余年在寧邸，故封建之事晚於諸王。

translations.literal: For more than ten years he remained at the Ning residence, and therefore his enfeoffment came later than that of the other princes.
translations.idiomatic: He spent more than ten years in the Ning household, and so received his princely title later than his brothers.

sentences.zh: 宮中常呼為十八郎。

translations.literal: Within the palace he was commonly called the Eighteenth Lord.
translations.idiomatic: In the palace they called him the Eighteenth Lord.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，封為壽王，始入宮中。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shou and first entered the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Shou and at last came to live within the palace.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領益州大都督、劍南節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he held in title the post of grand governor of Yizhou and military commissioner of Jiannan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was named grand governor of Yizhou in absentia and military commissioner over Jiannan.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，加開府儀同三司，改名瑁。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and renamed Mao.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff and was renamed Mao.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，惠妃薨，葬以後禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year Consort Hui died and was buried with the rites due a consort.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 Consort Wu Hui died and was buried with the honors owed a consort.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，讓帝薨，瑁請制服，以報乳養之恩，玄宗從之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year the Prince of Rang died; Mao requested mourning garments to repay the grace of being nursed and raised; Xuanzong consented.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 29 the Prince of Rang died; Mao asked leave to wear mourning in gratitude for the milk and years given him, and Xuanzong granted it.

sentences.zh: 瑁，天寶中有子封為王者二人：懷為濟陽郡王，偡為廣陽郡王、鴻臚卿同正員。

translations.literal: Mao, during the Tianbao period, had two sons enfeoffed as kings: Huai as Prince of Jiyang commandery, and Si as Prince of Guangyang commandery and acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao Mao had two sons created princes: Huai as Prince of Jiyang, and Si as Prince of Guangyang with acting rank as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 唐法，親王食封八百戶，有至一千戶；

translations.literal: Under Tang law, princes of the blood received fief income of eight hundred households, with some reaching one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: By Tang statute, imperial princes drew income from eight hundred fief households, though some received as many as a thousand.

sentences.zh: 公主三百戶，長公主加三百戶，有至六百戶。

translations.literal: Princesses received three hundred households; elder princesses received an additional three hundred, with some reaching six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses were granted three hundred households; elder princesses received three hundred more, and some held as many as six hundred.

sentences.zh: 高宗朝以沛、英、豫王、太平公主武後所生，食逾於制。

translations.literal: In the reign of Emperor Gaozong, because the Princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping were born of Empress Wu, their fief income exceeded the regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, the Princes of Pei, Ying, and Yu and Princess Taiping, all children of Empress Wu, received fiefs above the prescribed limit.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，太平至一千二百戶。

translations.literal: In the Chuigong era, Taiping reached one thousand two hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: During Chuigong, Taiping's fief rose to twelve hundred households.

sentences.zh: 聖歷初，皇嗣封為相王，食封與太平同三千戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Shengli era, the heir apparent was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang, and his fief income was the same as Taiping's: three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Shengli, when the crown prince was made Prince of Xiang, his fief matched Taiping's at three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 長安中，壽春王兄弟五人，並賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: In the Chang'an era, the five brothers of the Prince of Shouchun were each granted three hundred households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chang'an period the five brothers of the Prince of Shouchun each received three hundred households of actual fief income.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，相府與太平同至五千戶，衛王三千戶，溫王二千戶，成王七百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong, the Xiang household and Taiping each reached five thousand households; the Prince of Wei three thousand; the Prince of Wen two thousand; the Prince of Cheng seven hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Shenlong the Xiang household and Taiping each reached five thousand households; the Prince of Wei held three thousand; the Prince of Wen, two thousand; the Prince of Cheng, seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 壽春王加四百戶，通前七百戶；

translations.literal: The Prince of Shouchun received an additional four hundred households, for seven hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shouchun gained four hundred more, seven hundred in total.

sentences.zh: 嗣雍、衡陽、臨淄、巴陵、中山各加二百戶，通前五百戶。

translations.literal: The heirs of Yong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan each received an additional two hundred households, for five hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: The heirs of Yong, Hengyang, Linzi, Baling, and Zhongshan each gained two hundred more, five hundred in all.

sentences.zh: 安樂初封二千戶，長寧一千五百戶，宣城、宜城、宣安各一千戶，相王女為縣主者各三百戶。

translations.literal: At first enfeoffment, Princess Anle received two thousand households; Changning one thousand five hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an each one thousand; daughters of the Prince of Xiang enfeoffed as district mistresses each three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At first creation Princess Anle received two thousand households; Changning, fifteen hundred; Xuancheng, Yicheng, and Xuan'an, a thousand each; the Prince of Xiang's daughters made district mistresses, three hundred each.

sentences.zh: 衛王尋升儲位，相府增至七千戶，太平至五千戶，安樂三千戶，長寧二千五百戶，宣城已下各二千戶。

translations.literal: The Prince of Wei soon ascended the throne as heir apparent; the Xiang household was increased to seven thousand households; Taiping reached five thousand; Anle three thousand; Changning two thousand five hundred; Xuancheng and those below each two thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Wei rose to heir apparent, the Xiang household was raised to seven thousand; Taiping stood at five thousand; Anle at three thousand; Changning at twenty-five hundred; Xuancheng and the rest at two thousand each.

sentences.zh: 相府、太平、長寧、安樂皆以七千為限，雖水旱亦不破損免，以正租庸充數。

translations.literal: The Xiang household, Taiping, Changning, and Anle all took seven thousand as the limit; even in flood or drought the amount was not reduced or remitted, and regular land tax and corvée labor were counted toward the quota.
translations.idiomatic: For the Xiang household, Taiping, Changning, and Anle seven thousand was the ceiling; neither flood nor drought could pare or forgive the grant, and regular land tax and corvée were reckoned toward the count.

sentences.zh: 唐隆元年，遺制以嗣雍王守禮、壽春王成器封為親王，各賜實封一千戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tanglong, by testamentary decree the heirs of Prince Yong Shouli and the Prince of Shouchun Chenqi were enfeoffed as imperial princes, each granted one thousand households of actual fief income.
translations.idiomatic: In Tanglong 1 a deathbed edict made Shouli, heir of Prince Yong, and Chenqi, Prince of Shouchun, full imperial princes, each with a thousand households of actual fief income.

sentences.zh: 開元之後，朝恩睦親，以寧府最長，封至五千五百戶；

translations.literal: After Kaiyuan, the court favored kin with grace; because the Ning household was eldest, its fief reached five thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: After Kaiyuan the court treated its kin with deliberate warmth; the Ning household, as eldest, received fifty-five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 岐、薛愛弟著勛，五千戶；

translations.literal: The Qi and Xue households, as beloved younger brothers with notable merit, received five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi and Xue households, favored brothers with clear merit, each drew five thousand.

sentences.zh: 申府以外家微，至四千戶；

translations.literal: The Shen household, because its maternal line was humble, received up to four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen household, its maternal line being low-born, reached four thousand.

sentences.zh: 邠府以外枝，至一千八百戶。

translations.literal: The Bin household, as a distant branch, received up to one thousand eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: The Bin household, a more distant branch, received up to eighteen hundred.

sentences.zh: 皇妹為公主者，食封一千戶，中宗女亦同。

translations.literal: Imperial younger sisters enfeoffed as princesses received fief income of one thousand households; daughters of Emperor Zhongzong were the same.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial sisters made princesses drew a thousand households; Zhongzong's daughters received the same.

sentences.zh: 其後，皇子封王者賜封二千戶，皇女為公主者賜封五百戶。

translations.literal: Thereafter, imperial sons enfeoffed as kings were granted fiefs of two thousand households; imperial daughters made princesses were granted five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, princes of the blood received two thousand households; imperial daughters made princesses, five hundred.

sentences.zh: 咸宜賜湯沐，以母惠妃封至一千戶，諸皇女為公主者，例加至一千戶。

translations.literal: Princess Xianyi received bath-and-income grants; because her mother was Consort Hui, her fief reached one thousand households; other imperial daughters made princesses were by precedent raised to one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Xianyi received bath-income grants; as Consort Wu Hui's daughter her fief rose to a thousand, and other imperial daughters made princesses were by precedent raised to the same.

sentences.zh: 其封自開元已來，皆約以三千為限。

translations.literal: From Kaiyuan onward, all fiefs were generally capped at about three thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: From Kaiyuan on, fiefs were in general held to a ceiling of roughly three thousand households.

sentences.zh: 延王玢，玄宗第二十子也，初名洄。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Bin was Emperor Xuanzong's twentieth son; his original name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yan Bin was Xuanzong's twentieth son; his birth name was Hui.

sentences.zh: 玢母即尚書右丞柳範孫也，最為名家，玄宗深重之。

translations.literal: Bin's mother was the granddaughter of Vice Director of the Right Secretariat Liu Fan; hers was the most eminent family, and Xuanzong held her in deep regard.
translations.idiomatic: Bin's mother was granddaughter to Liu Fan, vice director of the Right Secretariat; hers was among the greatest houses of the age, and Xuanzong esteemed her deeply.

sentences.zh: 玢亦仁愛，有學問。

translations.literal: Bin was also benevolent and loving, and possessed learning.
translations.idiomatic: Bin too was gentle of heart and learned in the classics.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年，封為延王。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遙領安西大都護、磧西節度大使。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held in title the post of grand protector of Anxi and military commissioner of Qixi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was given nominal command as grand protector of Anxi and military commissioner of Qixi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，加開府儀同三司，余如故，改名玢。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was additionally given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office; his other posts remained as before, and he was renamed Bin.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff while retaining his other titles, and was renamed Bin.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載，玄宗幸蜀，玢男女三十六人，不忍棄於道路，數日不及行在所，玄宗怒之；

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, when Xuanzong fled to Shu, Bin's thirty-six sons and daughters could not bear to abandon them on the road; for several days they did not reach the traveling court, and Xuanzong was angry with him.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 15, when Xuanzong fled to Shu, Bin would not leave his thirty-six children on the road. For days they failed to reach the emperor's camp, and Xuanzong grew furious.

sentences.zh: 賴漢中王瑀抗疏救之，聽歸於靈武。

translations.literal: Thanks to Prince of Hanzhong Yu's forceful memorial in his defense, he was permitted to return to Lingwu.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Prince of Hanzhong Yu submitted an urgent memorial in his defense was he allowed to return to Lingwu.

sentences.zh: 興元元年薨。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Xingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Xingyuan.

sentences.zh: 天寶末，封子倬彭城郡王、秘書監同正員，亻延平陽郡王、殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of the Tianbao era, two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Chuo as Prince of Pengcheng commandery and acting director of the Secretariat, and Yan as Prince of Pingyang commandery and acting director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Chuo as Prince of Pengcheng with acting rank as director of the Secretariat, and Yan as Prince of Pingyang with acting rank as director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 盛王琦，玄宗第二十一子也。

translations.literal: Prince of Sheng Qi was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-first son.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Sheng Qi was Xuanzong's twenty-first son.

sentences.zh: 壽王母弟，初名沐。

translations.literal: He was the younger brother of Prince of Shou Mao; his original name was Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He was a younger brother of Prince of Shou Mao; his birth name was Mu.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月，封為盛王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Sheng.

sentences.zh: 十五年，領揚州大都督。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he held the post of grand governor of Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 15 he was appointed grand governor of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十年，加開府儀同三司，余如故，改名琦。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, he was given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office; his other posts remained as before, and he was renamed Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 20 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff while retaining his other titles, and was renamed Qi.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五年六月，玄宗幸蜀，在路除琦為廣陵大都督，仍領江南東路及淮南河南等路節度支度采訪等使，以前江陵大都督府長史劉匯為之副，以廣陵長史李成式為副大使、兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, as Xuanzong fled to Shu on the road, Qi was removed from office and made grand governor of Guangling, while still holding the posts of commissioner of pacification, inspection, supply, and expenditure over Jiangnan East Route and Huainan, Henan, and other circuits; Liu Hui, former chief administrator of the Jiangling grand governorship, was made his deputy, and Li Chengshi, chief administrator of Guangling, was made deputy commissioner and concurrently censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianbao 15, while Xuanzong was fleeing to Shu, Qi was named grand governor of Guangling and commissioner of pacification, inspection, supply, and expenditure over Jiangnan East, Huainan, Henan, and related circuits. Liu Hui, former chief administrator at Jiangling, served as his deputy; Li Chengshi, chief administrator of Guangling, was deputy commissioner and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 琦竟不行。

translations.literal: Qi in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Qi never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 廣德二年四月薨，贈太傅。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth month of the second year of Guangde; he was posthumously made grand tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth month of Guangde 2 and was posthumously honored as grand tutor.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封王者二人：償真定郡王、太常卿同正員，佩封武都郡王、殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Chang as Prince of Zhending commandery and acting chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Pei as Prince of Wudu commandery and acting director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Chang as Prince of Zhending with acting rank as chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Pei as Prince of Wudu with acting rank as director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 濟王環，玄宗第二十二子也，初名溢。

translations.literal: Prince of Ji Huan was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-second son; his original name was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Ji Huan was Xuanzong's twenty-second son; his birth name was Yi.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封濟王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Ji.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，其月改名環。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office; that same month he was renamed Huan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff, and that month he was renamed Huan.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人，傃為永嘉郡王、衛尉卿同正員，俛為平樂郡王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Su as Prince of Yongjia commandery and acting minister of the Guards, and Mian as Prince of Pingle commandery and acting commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Su as Prince of Yongjia with acting rank as minister of the Guards, and Mian as Prince of Pingle with acting rank as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 信王瑝，玄宗第二十三子也，初名沔。

translations.literal: Prince of Xin Huang was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-third son; his original name was Mian.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Xin Huang was Xuanzong's twenty-third son; his birth name was Mian.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為信王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xin.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Xin.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，仍改名瑝。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and was renamed Huang.
