translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff and was renamed Huang.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人：亻冬為新安郡王、太常卿同正員，倜為晉陵郡王、光祿卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Dong as Prince of Xin'an commandery and acting chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Tong as Prince of Jinling commandery and acting commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Dong as Prince of Xin'an with acting rank as chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Tong as Prince of Jinling with acting rank as commissioner of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 義王玭，玄宗第二十四子也，初名漼。

translations.literal: Prince of Yi Ni was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-fourth son; his original name was Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Yi Ni was Xuanzong's twenty-fourth son; his birth name was Cui.

sentences.zh: 開元十三年三月，封為義王。

translations.literal: In the third month of the thirteenth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 13 he was created Prince of Yi.

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，授開府儀同三司，仍改名玭。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office and was renamed Ni.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff and was renamed Ni.

sentences.zh: 天寶末有子封為王者二人：儀為舞陽郡王、太仆卿同正員，僇為高密郡王、宗正卿同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao two sons were enfeoffed as princes: Yi as Prince of Wuyang commandery and acting minister of the Stud, and Lu as Prince of Gaomi commandery and acting director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Yi as Prince of Wuyang with acting rank as minister of the Stud, and Lu as Prince of Gaomi with acting rank as director of the Imperial Clan Court.

sentences.zh: 陳王珪，玄宗第二十五子也，初名渙。

translations.literal: Prince of Chen Gui was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-fifth son; his original name was Huan.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chen Gui was Xuanzong's twenty-fifth son; his birth name was Huan.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為陳王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was created Prince of Chen.

sentences.zh: 二十四年三月改名珪。

translations.literal: In the third month of the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Gui.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Gui.

sentences.zh: 天寶末男女二十一人，封為王者二人：佗為臨淮郡王、太常卿同正員，佼為安陽王、殿中監同正員。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he had twenty-one sons and daughters; two were enfeoffed as princes: Tuo as Prince of Linhuai commandery and acting chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Jiao as Prince of Anyang and acting director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tianbao he had twenty-one children; two sons were created princes: Tuo as Prince of Linhuai with acting rank as chancellor of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and Jiao as Prince of Anyang with acting rank as director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 豐王珙，玄宗第二十六子也，初名澄。

translations.literal: Prince of Feng Gong was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-sixth son; his original name was Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Feng Gong was Xuanzong's twenty-sixth son; his birth name was Cheng.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為豐王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Feng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was created Prince of Feng.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月改名珙。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Gong.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Gong.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五年六月，玄宗幸蜀，至扶風郡，授珙武威郡都督，仍領河西隴右安西北庭等路節度支度采訪使；

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fifteenth year of Tianbao, as Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Fufeng commandery, Gong was appointed governor of Wuwei commandery and still held the posts of commissioner of pacification, supply, and inspection over Hexi, Longyou, Anbei, and Beiting circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of Tianbao 15, as Xuanzong fled to Shu and reached Fufeng, Gong was named governor of Wuwei and commissioner of pacification, supply, and inspection over Hexi, Longyou, Anbei, and Beiting.

sentences.zh: 以隴右太守鄧景山為之副，兼武威長史、御史中丞，充都副大使。

translations.literal: Deng Jingshan, governor of Longyou, was made his deputy, and concurrently chief administrator of Wuwei, censor-in-chief, and deputy commissioner-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Jingshan, governor of Longyou, served as his deputy, and also as chief administrator of Wuwei, censor-in-chief, and deputy commissioner-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 珙竟不行。

translations.literal: Gong in the end did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Gong never took up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 廣德元年十月，吐蕃淩逼上都，上將幸陜州，自苑中而出，騎從半渡浐水。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the first year of Guangde, when the Tibetans pressed close upon the upper capital, the emperor was about to go to Shaanzhou and left through the park; his mounted escort was halfway across the Chan River.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Guangde 1, as Tibetans threatened the capital, the emperor prepared to flee to Shaanzhou and rode out through the imperial park; his escort was halfway across the Chan River.

sentences.zh: 將軍王懷忠遂閉苑門，橫截五百余騎，擁十宅諸王西投吐蕃。

translations.literal: General Wang Huaizhong then closed the park gates, cut off more than five hundred horsemen, and led the princes of the Ten Residences west to surrender to the Tibetans.
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Huaizhong shut the park gates, intercepted more than five hundred riders, and led the princes of the Ten Residences west toward the Tibetans.

sentences.zh: 至城西，適遇元帥郭子儀，懷忠謂子儀曰：「主上東遷，社稷無主，萬國颙颙，何所瞻仰！

translations.literal: When they reached the west of the city, they happened upon the commander-in-chief Guo Ziyi. Huaizhong said to Ziyi, "The sovereign has moved east; the altars of state are without a master; the myriad states look on with upturned faces—where shall they turn their gaze?
translations.idiomatic: At the west gate they met the commander-in-chief Guo Ziyi. Huaizhong told him, "The emperor has gone east; the realm has no ruler; all the world looks up in longing—whom shall they follow?

sentences.zh: 今仆奉諸王等西奔，以副天下之望。

translations.literal: Now your servant leads these princes west in flight to answer the hope of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: I am taking these princes west to meet the people's expectation.

sentences.zh: 令公身為元帥，廢置在手，何不行冊立之事乎？

translations.literal: You, sir, are the commander-in-chief; enthronement and deposition are in your hand—why not perform the rite of investiture?
translations.idiomatic: You stand as commander-in-chief; enthronement and deposition rest in your hands—why not carry out an investiture?

sentences.zh: 」子儀未及對，珙遂越次而言曰：「令公作何語，何不言也？

translations.literal: " Before Ziyi could reply, Gong spoke out of turn and said, "What words are these, Commander? Why do you not speak?
translations.idiomatic: " Before Ziyi could answer, Gong broke in: "What talk is this, Commander? Why do you say nothing?

sentences.zh: 」行軍司馬王延昌責之曰：「主上雖蒙塵於外，聖德欽明，王身為籓翰，何乃發狂悖之詞也？

translations.literal: " The marching army judge Wang Yanchang rebuked him, saying, "Although the sovereign suffers dust abroad, his sagely virtue is revered and bright. Your Highness serves as a bulwark of the realm—how can you utter words of mad treason?
translations.idiomatic: " The army judge Wang Yanchang rebuked him: "Though the emperor is abroad in hardship, his virtue remains clear. You are a prince of the realm—how dare you speak such treasonous words?

sentences.zh: 延昌當奏聞於上。

translations.literal: Yanchang will memorialize this to the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: I shall report this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 」子儀又數讓之，命軍士領之盡赴行在。

translations.literal: " Ziyi again repeatedly reproved him and ordered soldiers to escort them all to the traveling court.
translations.idiomatic: " Ziyi reproved him again and again and ordered troops to escort them all to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 潼關謁見，上不之責，珙歸幕次，詞又不順。

translations.literal: At Tong Pass they had audience; the emperor did not blame him, but when Gong returned to his quarters his words were again improper.
translations.idiomatic: They presented themselves at Tong Pass; the emperor did not rebuke him at once, but back in his quarters Gong spoke improperly again.

sentences.zh: 群臣恐遂為亂，請除之，遂賜死。

translations.literal: The ministers feared he would soon stir rebellion and asked that he be removed; he was then granted death.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing he would soon raise a revolt, the ministers asked that he be put to death, and the court granted it.

sentences.zh: 天寶中有子二人為王：佻齊安郡王、宗正卿同正員，伷宜春郡王、鴻臚卿同正員。

translations.literal: During Tianbao he had two sons enfeoffed as princes: Tiao as Prince of Qi'an commandery and acting director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Zhou as Prince of Yichun commandery and acting director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianbao two of his sons were created princes: Tiao as Prince of Qi'an with acting rank as director of the Imperial Clan Court, and Zhou as Prince of Yichun with acting rank as director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 恆王瑱，玄宗第二十七子也，初名潓。

translations.literal: Prince of Heng Zhen was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-seventh son; his original name was Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Heng Zhen was Xuanzong's twenty-seventh son; his birth name was Hui.

sentences.zh: 開元二十三年七月，封為恆王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Heng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was created Prince of Heng.

sentences.zh: 性好道，常服道士衣。

translations.literal: He was fond of the Way and often wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: He loved the Way and often dressed as a Daoist priest.

sentences.zh: 授右衛大將軍，加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was appointed great general of the Right Guard and given the rank of Grandee of the First Order with the privilege of an independent office.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed great general of the Right Guard and granted the rank of Grandee of the First Order with an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月改名瑱。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Zhen.

sentences.zh: 天寶十五載，從幸巴蜀，不復衣道士衣矣。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Tianbao, he followed the emperor in flight to Ba-Shu and no longer wore Daoist robes.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 15 he accompanied the flight to Ba-Shu and put aside his Daoist dress.

sentences.zh: 涼王璿，玄宗第二十九子也，初名漎。

translations.literal: Prince of Liang Xuan was Emperor Xuanzong's twenty-ninth son; his original name was Long.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Liang Xuan was Xuanzong's twenty-ninth son; his birth name was Long.

sentences.zh: 母武賢儀，則天時高平王重規女也，開元中入宮中，號為「小武妃」。

translations.literal: His mother was Lady Wu Xianyi, daughter of Prince of Gaoping Chonggui in the time of Wu Zetian; in the Kaiyuan era she entered the palace and was called "Little Consort Wu."
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Wu Xianyi, daughter of Prince of Gaoping Chonggui from Wu Zetian's time; in Kaiyuan she entered the palace and was known as "Little Consort Wu."

sentences.zh: 二十三年七月，封為涼王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-third year, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 23 he was created Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月，改名璿。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Xuan.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，高宗為晉王，以文德皇后最少子，後崩後累年，太宗憐之，不令出閣，至立為太子。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the Zhenguan era, when Gaozong was Prince of Jin, as the youngest son of Empress Wende, after the empress died and years passed, Taizong pitied him and would not let him leave the palace until he was installed as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era, when Gaozong was Prince of Jin—the youngest son of Empress Wende—Taizong kept him in the palace for years after the empress's death out of pity, and only then named him heir.

sentences.zh: 高宗朝，睿宗為豫王，雖成長，亦以則天最小子，不令出閣。

translations.literal: In the Gaozong era, when Ruizong was Prince of Yu, though he had grown up, because he was Wu Zetian's youngest son he was likewise not let leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong, Ruizong as Prince of Yu was also kept in the palace though fully grown, for he was Wu Zetian's youngest son.

sentences.zh: 及至聖歷初，封為相王，始出閣。

translations.literal: Only at the beginning of the Shengli era, when he was enfeoffed as Prince of Xiang, did he first leave the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the opening of Shengli, when he was made Prince of Xiang, did he first leave the inner quarters.

sentences.zh: 中宗時，以譙王重福失愛，出遷外籓，衛王重俊為太子，入與成王千里等起兵，將誅韋後，故溫王重茂雖年十六七，竟亦居中。

translations.literal: In the Zhongzong era, because Prince of Qiao Chongfu had lost favor and was sent out to a distant fief, and Prince of Wei Chongjun was heir apparent and joined Prince of Cheng Qianli and others in raising troops to execute Empress Wei, Prince of Wen Chongmao, though only sixteen or seventeen, was nevertheless kept within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhongzong, Prince of Qiao Chongfu, out of favor, was sent to a distant fief; Prince of Wei Chongjun, as heir, joined Prince of Cheng Qianli in arms against Empress Wei—yet Prince of Wen Chongmao, though only sixteen or seventeen, was still kept inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 先天之後，皇子幼則居內，東封年，以漸成長，乃於安國寺東附苑城同為大宅，分院居，為十王宅。

translations.literal: After the Xiantian era, when princes were young they dwelt within; in the year of the eastern Feng sacrifice, as they gradually grew, great residences were built east of Anguo Temple adjoining the park wall, divided into courtyards—the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiantian, young princes lived within the palace. When they grew older, at the time of the eastern Feng rite, great mansions were built east of Anguo Temple against the park wall, divided into courtyards—the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 令中官押之，於夾城中起居，每日家令進膳。

translations.literal: Eunuchs were assigned to supervise them; they lived in the walled lane, and each day the household stewards brought meals.
translations.idiomatic: Eunuchs supervised them in a walled lane; household stewards delivered meals each day.

sentences.zh: 又引詞學工書之人入教，謂之侍讀。

translations.literal: Men skilled in letters and calligraphy were also brought in to teach them, called lecturing companions.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars skilled in letters and calligraphy were brought in to instruct them as lecturing companions.

sentences.zh: 十王，謂慶、忠、棣、鄂、榮、光、儀、潁、永、延、濟，蓋舉全數。

translations.literal: The ten princes were Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, and Yan, and Ji—names standing for the full number.
translations.idiomatic: The "ten princes" meant Qing, Zhong, Di, E, Rong, Guang, Yi, Ying, Yong, Yan, and Ji—a round figure for the whole group.

sentences.zh: 其後，盛、儀、壽、陳、豐、恆、涼六王又就封，入內宅。

translations.literal: Later, when Princes of Sheng, Yi, Shou, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang were enfeoffed, they too entered the inner residence.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Princes of Sheng, Yi, Shou, Chen, Feng, Heng, and Liang were created, they too moved into the inner residence.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，鄂、光得罪，忠繼大統，天寶中，慶、棣又歿，唯榮、儀等十四王居院，而府幕列於外坊，時通名起居而已。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year, Princes of E and Guang fell from favor; Zhong succeeded to the great succession; in the Tianbao era, Princes of Qing and Di also died; only Princes of Rong, Yi, and fourteen others remained in the courtyard, while their staff offices were set in the outer lanes and at the time only sent in their names for daily attendance.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 25 Princes E and Guang were disgraced; Zhong became heir; in Tianbao Princes Qing and Di died. Only Rong, Yi, and fourteen others remained in the residence, their staff housed in outer lanes and sending in names for attendance.

sentences.zh: 外諸孫成長，又於十宅外置百孫院。

translations.literal: As imperial grandsons abroad grew up, a Hundred Grandsons' Court was also established outside the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial grandsons abroad came of age, a Hundred Grandsons' Court was added outside the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 每歲幸華清宮，宮側亦有十王院、百孫院。

translations.literal: Each year when the emperor visited Huaqing Palace, there were also Ten Princes' and Hundred Grandsons' courts beside the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Each year at Huaqing Palace there were companion residences for the ten princes and hundred grandsons.

sentences.zh: 宮人每院四百，百孫院三四十人。

translations.literal: Each princely courtyard had four hundred palace women; the Hundred Grandsons' Court had thirty or forty.
translations.idiomatic: Each princely courtyard held four hundred palace women; the Hundred Grandsons' Court, thirty or forty.

sentences.zh: 又於宮中置維城庫，諸王月俸物，約之而給用。

translations.literal: Within the palace a Weicheng Storehouse was also established; the princes' monthly allowances were rationed and issued from it.
translations.idiomatic: A Weicheng storehouse in the palace rationed and issued the princes' monthly allowances.

sentences.zh: 諸孫納妃嫁女，亦就十宅中。

translations.literal: When grandsons took consorts or granddaughters married, the ceremonies also took place within the Ten Princes' Residence.
translations.idiomatic: Grandsons' weddings and granddaughters' marriages were likewise held in the Ten Princes' Residence.

sentences.zh: 太子不居於東宮，但居於乘輿所幸之別院。

translations.literal: The heir apparent did not dwell in the Eastern Palace but lived in whatever separate residence the imperial carriage favored.
translations.idiomatic: The heir did not live in the Eastern Palace but in whichever secondary residence the emperor favored.

sentences.zh: 太子亦分院而居，婚嫁則同親王、公主，在於崇仁之禮院。

translations.literal: The heir also lived in a separate courtyard; marriages were handled like those of imperial princes and princesses, in the ritual hall of Chongren.
translations.idiomatic: The heir too had a separate courtyard; weddings followed the same rites as for princes and princesses in the Chongren ritual hall.

sentences.zh: 汴哀王璥，玄宗第三十子也，初名滔。

translations.literal: Prince of Bian Aihuan Jin was Emperor Xuanzong's thirtieth son; his original name was Tao.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Bian Aihuan Jin was Xuanzong's thirtieth son; his birth name was Tao.

sentences.zh: 開元二十五年七月，封為汴王。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the twenty-fifth year of Kaiyuan, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Kaiyuan 25 he was created Prince of Bian.

sentences.zh: 二十四年二月，改名璥，以其月薨。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twenty-fourth year, he was renamed Jin, and in that same month he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Kaiyuan 24 he was renamed Jin and died that same month.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：前史有云：「母愛者子抱」，太子瑛之廢，有由然矣。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The former histories say, "Whom the mother loves, the child embraces"—the deposing of Crown Prince Ying indeed had its causes.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Earlier histories say, "Whom the mother loves, the child embraces." Crown Prince Ying's deposition had its reasons.

sentences.zh: 琬為元帥，不幸遽薨，豈天啟亂階，何失眾望之速也！

translations.literal: Wan was made commander-in-chief but unfortunately died suddenly—was Heaven opening the gate to disorder? How swiftly he lost the people's hope!
translations.idiomatic: Wan was named commander-in-chief only to die at once—did Heaven itself open the way to rebellion? How quickly the people's hopes were dashed.

sentences.zh: 永王璘，父在蜀城，兄居靈武，不能立忠孝之節，為社稷之謀，而乃聚兵江上，規為己利，不義不昵，以災其身，《書》所謂「自作孽，不可逭」也。

translations.literal: Prince Yong Lin: his father was in the Shu cities and his elder brother at Lingwu; he could not establish loyalty and filial piety or plan for the altars of state, but instead gathered troops on the river and schemed for his own profit—neither righteous nor intimate, bringing disaster on himself. As the Documents say, "He who brings calamity on himself cannot escape it."
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yong Lin: with his father in Shu and his brother at Lingwu, he failed in loyalty and filial piety and schemed not for the realm but to gather armies on the Yangtze for his own gain—unrighteous and disloyal, he brought ruin on himself. The Documents say, "He who courts disaster cannot escape it."

sentences.zh: 豐王珙因緣厄運，竊有覬覦，不慎樞機，自貽伊咎，悲矣！

translations.literal: Prince of Feng Gong, riding on hard fortune, secretly harbored ambitious designs; heedless of the pivot of power, he brought ruin on himself—lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Feng Gong, caught in calamitous times, secretly nursed imperial ambitions; careless of the levers of state, he destroyed himself—a tragedy.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：《螽斯》之詠，樂有子孫。

translations.literal: The encomium says: The ode of the Katydids celebrates the joy of having sons and grandsons.
translations.idiomatic: The encomium reads: The Katydids ode celebrates the blessing of sons and grandsons.

sentences.zh: 用建籓屏，以崇本根。

translations.literal: They are used to build the screen of the realm and to strengthen the root.
translations.idiomatic: They are made a bulwark of the realm to fortify the dynastic root.

sentences.zh: 讒勝瑛廢，恩移至尊。

translations.literal: Slander overcame Ying's deposition; favor shifted the supreme seat.
translations.idiomatic: Slander toppled Ying; favor moved the throne itself.

sentences.zh: 盜熾琬卒，情乖萬民。

translations.literal: Rebellion flared and Wan died; hearts turned from the myriad people.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion rose and Wan perished; the people's hearts fell away.

sentences.zh: 口禍豐珙，自災永璘。

translations.literal: The mouth's calamity struck Feng Gong; Yong Lin brought disaster on himself.
translations.idiomatic: Reckless speech destroyed Feng Gong; Yong Lin wrought his own ruin.

sentences.zh: 惜乎二胤，不如仁人。

translations.literal: Pity these two heirs—they were not men of humanity.
translations.idiomatic: Pity these two princes: they were no true gentlemen.
